summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of endometriosis and bipolar disorder was admitted for acute worsening of chronic left lower quadrant abdominal pain, radiating to the rectum and left leg, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She had recently been seen in the ED for similar symptoms without relief from home medications. CT imaging showed no acute abdominal or pelvic pathology, though small non-obstructing kidney stones were noted. Pain was managed with initiation of indomethacin and adjustments to her gabapentin and tizanidine doses per pain team recommendations. Her bipolar disorder, asthma, and GERD remained stable on home medications. She was discharged home after 1.5 days with a plan to continue pain medications, complete a two-week course of indomethacin with kidney function monitoring, and follow up with the pain clinic and OB/GYN.
